title: Hindustan Unilever Ltd - 500696 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: HUL Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue grew 8% with 7% USG led by volumes; EBITDA margin 23.7% at top of guidance; FY27 guided better than FY26.
summary.overview: March quarter 2026 consolidated revenue rose 8% with 7% underlying sales growth (USG), the company's highest quarterly growth in 12 quarters, driven mainly by volume (UVG 6%). EBITDA grew 6% with margin at 23.7%, the higher end of guidance, while PAT before exceptionals was Rs 2,711 crore (+4%); reported PAT rose 20% helped by the Nutritionalab divestment versus an OZiva fair-value base effect. For FY26, turnover was Rs 63,763 crore with 5% USG and 4% UVG, and the second half outpaced the first; EBITDA grew 2% at a 23.6% margin. Management flagged a sharp March-onward rise in crude-linked input costs (8-10% material cost inflation) from the Middle East crisis and has taken 2-5% price increases, with more pricing possible.

financial_highlights.change: YoY; includes Nutritionalab divestment gain, offset by OZiva fair-value base effect

segments.name: Home Care
segments.commentary: Q4 USG 9% on high-single-digit UVG, strongest in 11 quarters; liquids grew double digit and crossed Rs 4,000 crore turnover. FY26 USG 4%.

segments.name: Beauty & Wellbeing
segments.commentary: Q4 USG 8% on mid-single-digit UVG; hair care grew strong double digit; premium skin care grew double digit while mass skin (Glow & Lovely, talc) was subdued. FY26 USG 6%. Minimalist ARR about Rs 850 crore; Simple ARR above Rs 160 crore.

segments.name: Personal Care
segments.commentary: Q4 USG 5%, pricing-led; skin cleansing grew high single digit (highest in 12 quarters) and premium cleansing bars grew double-digit volume. Oral care grew low single digit. FY26 USG 4%.

segments.name: Foods
segments.commentary: Q4 USG 5% on high-single-digit UVG; coffee grew double digit, tea grew low-single-digit volume, lifestyle nutrition grew double digit. FY26 USG 5% on mid-single-digit UVG.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated top line expected to be better than FY26 (USG basis), despite Middle East and currency volatility.
Mid-term EBITDA margin guidance kept at 22.5% to 23.5%; management expects Q1 FY27 to be at the lower end given cost pressure.

Material cost inflation of 8-10% seen for the June quarter; 2-5% price increases taken so far, with further calibrated price increases in Fabric Wash and Household Care in June quarter and beyond if costs persist.
Full-year FY27 pricing not guided; management said it is too difficult to give a number.
A&P spend stepped up by Rs 270 crore in absolute terms in FY26; non-working media being optimised while core brands stay fully funded.
capex_capacity: Rs 2,000 crore capex signed off for premium formats (liquids in Home Care, Personal Care and Beauty); timeline not specified.
Rs 3,500 crore deployed in FY26 on bolt-on acquisitions including Minimalist and OZiva.
Direct General Trade coverage increased by around 2 lakh outlets in FY26; specialty retail (open format stores, chemists, cosmetic stores) infrastructure being built.
Quick Commerce customer availability up about 1,400 basis points (as shared last quarter); a dedicated Quick Commerce organisation created.
Management said it remains open to bolt-on acquisitions.
demand_pricing: Demand described as stable; rural and urban demand growing at roughly equal rates in FY26.
No pre-buying by trade ahead of March/April price increases; no restocking effect in Q4 per management.
Home Care negative UPG is anniversarising; tea volumes low-single-digit with deflation in pricing cited as the cause.
Bodywash share up about 400 bps (Nielsen-based); body wash and premium skin cleansing growing double digit.

Monsoon forecast at 92% of normal; management cited higher reservoir levels, MSP increases of 5-6%, and record government grain stocks as offsets, and expects no rural demand impact unless rainfall falls below 85%.

qa_highlights.question: Is growth driven by volume gains after GST cuts, and what are the drivers of UVG?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited three volume buckets: market development (liquids Rs 4,000 crore, mostly volumetric), share gains on core brands, and channel capability build-out; it said elasticity gains are being reinvested.

qa_highlights.question: How confident is management on margins amid input cost volatility, and would volume priority mean margin risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost inflation of 8-10% on material basket versus 2-5% pricing taken so far; savings funnel accelerated; margin band of 22.5-23.5% retained, with lower end likely in the current quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why are Home Care price hikes more modest than in the FY23 cycle?
qa_highlights.answer: Current crude-driven inflation is seen as volatile and geopolitical rather than structural, so price increases are being taken in steps; further hikes will follow if costs persist.

qa_highlights.question: Why is mass skin care dragging Beauty & Wellbeing and what is being done?
qa_highlights.answer: Glow & Lovely and talc were subdued (talc hit by seasonal weakness in March); premium skin care is growing double digit with a premium skin portfolio ARR near Rs 1,400 crore; focus on democratising new formats like sunscreen and light moisturisers.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 pricing outlook and Minimalist size?
qa_highlights.answer: No full-year pricing number given; Minimalist ARR is about Rs 850 crore; cosmetics sub-category growth not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Is there Lifestyle Nutrition sustainability given milk inflation risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Horlicks is consumed in water as well as milk, is focusing on nutrition benefits, and new segments (RTD, protein, Horlicks Superfoods relaunch) are still small with headroom.

risks_watch: Input cost inflation of 8-10% with crude volatility (Brent cited between $85 and $120) and rupee depreciation; pricing lag could pressure margins below the 22.5-23.5% band.
Monsoon and El Nino risk to H2 rural demand; management's threshold is rainfall below 85%.
Mass skin care and Personal Care volume weakness; Personal Care grew only 5% and is pricing-led.
Price elasticity and possible down-trading if further price increases are taken; Home Care rebalancing of price and volume expected in the short term.
Horlicks/Boost recovery still early; Horlicks Superfoods national rollout and protein launch pending.
Foods remains outside the Unilever transaction perimeter; questions on the strategy alignment were addressed.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume-led momentum and FY27 top-line growth, but cautious on margins and pricing, repeatedly describing the cost environment as volatile and short-term. Management declined to split the portfolio into growth and core buckets or give full-year pricing and cosmetics growth figures.
key_quotes: Importantly, this represents our highest quarterly growth in 12 quarters, reflecting both the ongoing transformation of our portfolio and the step-up of on-ground execution.

So, we have said a band of 22.5% to 23.5%. Now that band allows us to operate at sometimes a higher end of the band when things are favourable in terms of cost scenario, and maybe lower end of the band when things are not so favourable.
Competitive volume-led growth is our number one priority.

adds.what: Rs 2,000 crore capex signed off to expand capacity in premium formats (liquids in Home Care, Personal Care and Beauty); timeline not specified

growth.why: Management expects FY27 top line better than FY26 on a USG basis (FY26 USG 5%) with Q4 USG at 7% and exit-rate momentum, backed by volume growth (UVG 6% in Q4), 2-5% price increases taken, and a Rs 2,000 crore premium-format capex signed off with no timeline; mid-term EBITDA margin band held at 22.5-23.5%.
